shape: the three downstream analysis sub-stages (rnaseq-de, scrna-qc-cluster, spatial-cluster-count): reply, STATUS gate, check on a resolved input, prepare, submit, status and hand-off, later status, collect naming the supplier, history

inputs: the config and the input the router resolved, carried in the conversation
1.rung_why: T1 is sent before any helper runs, so its values come from the model reading files and remembering the router's resolution (D20).

2.rung_why: As in the wrapper shape: five STATUS values have no stated entry point.

unsaid.decision: Where to resume a sub-stage whose STATUS is VALIDATING, ARTIFACT_MISSING, STALE or FAILED
unsaid.goes_wrong: Step 2 stops only on SUBMITTED, RUNNING or COMPLETE, so read literally the other states fall through to check, prepare and submit; only step 7's 'On a later invocation' implies jumping to the status call and collect. A literal reading re-prepares a finished run, rewriting its params and reproducibility manifest, and tries to submit it again
unsaid.why_rank: Wasted work and a rewritten provenance file rather than a wrong result: the executor's duplicate-submission refusal and collect's gates stand behind it
unsaid.fix: Step 2 branches every STATUS value to its step, as the router's steps 6-9 do; better, the wrapper reports the next action from STATUS

inputs: the h5ad path the router resolved, carried in the conversation
3.rung_why: The check is code, but its input path is whatever the model carried over from the router's resolution; no step here resolves it.

unsaid.decision: Which input path to pass, and which sub-stage to name as its supplier at collect
unsaid.goes_wrong: The router resolves the inputs at its step 9 and the sub-stage contract starts afresh; the path and the supplying sub-stage travel only in the conversation, so the model carries or re-derives them. A wrong --h5ad-from or --counts-from records the wrong provenance; a wrong path feeds the wrong object
unsaid.why_rank: collect cross-checks counts against the samplesheet and rnaseq-de's prepare refuses a non-canonical design, so most wrong inputs are caught; the provenance line is not
unsaid.fix: Each sub-stage resolves its own inputs (rnaseq-de already does at its step 3) and collect derives the supplier from the resolver

3.note: Exit 3 (no such project) has no branch.

inputs: the resolved input and the config
4.note: The extractor's static exit 2 (wrapperlib.py:925, scripts tree not generated-only) is reachable here (downstream-v2 key) and has no branch; exit 3 has none either.

inputs: the dataset row and executor descriptor (venue preflight)
5.evidence: the submission record and STATUS SUBMITTED, when it succeeds
controls: run markers bound to script hashes
5.rung_why: As in the wrapper shape: no branch for a refused submission.

unsaid.decision: What to do when the executor refuses the submission
unsaid.goes_wrong: No step branches on submit's exit: each sub-stage's submit step says only to capture job_id before T2 announces 'Submitted as job <job_id>', and stage 03's step 7 handles only an approval refusal. A venue-preflight refusal (unclassified or expired dataset, a route or memory rule) or a duplicate-submission refusal exits 1 or 2 with no branch, so the model either reports a submission that did not happen or improvises, for example by editing the config's memory declaration until the venue rule passes
unsaid.why_rank: The venue rules are a data-policy gate; an improvised way past one is a breach only a reader of the transcript would see
unsaid.fix: Branch on submit's exit: 1 or 2 sends the failure template with the refusal verbatim and stops; never change config to pass a venue rule

unsaid.decision: How to spell a call the guard accepts only through the dispatcher
unsaid.goes_wrong: In a workspace holding any non-public project, the guard refuses the direct spelling of submit, status, the resolver and the DE wrapper, which is how every contract writes them, and accepts only tool_call.py with JSON arguments; the model translates each call itself
unsaid.why_rank: The refusal names the dispatcher, so the road is recoverable, but the argument translation is the model's
unsaid.fix: Contracts spell door calls through the dispatcher, or the guard maps the direct spelling for a public project

7.evidence: STATUS refreshed by the status call
7.rung_why: As in the wrapper shape (W-poll); here 'not yet terminal' is the only branch, so a FAILED status falls to collect, whose gate refuses it (D21).

unsaid.decision: When to refresh a submitted job's STATUS, and who does it
unsaid.goes_wrong: Only executorlib.py status moves STATUS from SUBMITTED to VALIDATING, but the router stops on SUBMITTED or RUNNING and sends the user to squeue, and every sub-stage's step 2 stops too; the sub-stage's status call is reached only if the model decides to poll on its own or the user runs a status command a template showed them. A finished job can look 'still running' indefinitely, or the model polls in a loop the scope forbids
unsaid.why_rank: A stall, not a wrong result, and a visible one; but every assay passes through it
unsaid.fix: The router calls status once before routing a SUBMITTED or RUNNING sub-stage

9.rung_why: Copying is written, but the date has no source the agent can reach.

unsaid.decision: What today's date is, for the HISTORY.md entry
unsaid.goes_wrong: The helper leaves `<ISO-8601 date>` for the agent to replace, and no registered command reads the clock, so the permanent record carries the model's belief about the date
unsaid.why_rank: A wrong date misleads a later reader of the record but changes no result; nothing ever checks it
unsaid.fix: The helper stamps the date (it already imports datetime) and appends the entry itself
